```{r}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE
)
has_dials <- requireNamespace("dials", quietly = TRUE)
has_parsnip <- requireNamespace("parsnip", quietly = TRUE)
```

dsprrr integrates with tidymodels in three places: scoring module predictions
with `yardstick`, building parameter grids for `optimize_grid()` with `dials`,
and wrapping zero-shot prediction modules in the `llm_predict()` `parsnip`
model specification.

```{r setup}
#| eval: true
#| message: false
library(dsprrr)
```

## Score predictions with yardstick

Run the module over a data frame with `run_dataset()`, which keeps every column
and adds a `result` list-column. Turn the predicted field into a factor with
the truth's levels, and any `yardstick` metric works:

```{r}
library(yardstick)

reviews <- tibble::tibble(
  text = c("Arrived broken.", "Works great.", "It's a chair."),
  sentiment = factor(c("negative", "positive", "neutral"))
)
classify <- module(
  signature("text -> sentiment: enum('negative', 'neutral', 'positive')")
)

scored <- run_dataset(
  classify,
  reviews,
  .llm = ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-luna")
)
scored$.pred_class <- factor(
  vapply(
    scored$result,
    \(r) if (is.list(r)) r$sentiment else NA_character_,
    character(1)
  ),
  levels = levels(scored$sentiment)
)

accuracy(scored, truth = sentiment, estimate = .pred_class)
conf_mat(scored, truth = sentiment, estimate = .pred_class)
```

A row whose call failed holds `NA` in `result`, hence the `is.list()` check.
Setting `levels` matters: `yardstick` refuses a prediction factor whose levels
differ from the truth's, which happens whenever some class is never predicted.

## Build grids with dials

`temperature()`, `top_p()`, and `reasoning_effort()` are `dials` parameter
objects (`temperature()` and `top_p()` default to `[0, 1]`):

```{r dials-params}
#| eval: !expr has_dials
temperature()
reasoning_effort()
dials::grid_regular(temperature(), levels = 3)
```

`module_parameters()` suggests a `dials` parameter set for a module, swapping
`temperature`/`top_p` for `reasoning_effort` when `model` looks like a
reasoning model (pass `include` to pick only the knobs you want):

```{r module-params}
#| eval: !expr has_dials
classify <- module(
  signature("text -> sentiment: enum('negative', 'neutral', 'positive')")
)
knobs <- c("temperature", "top_p", "reasoning_effort")
module_parameters(classify, model = "claude-sonnet-4-5", include = knobs)
module_parameters(classify, model = "gpt-6-luna", include = knobs)
```

`optimize_grid()` accepts a `dials` grid directly, or a `dials::parameters()`
set to build one from. It evaluates each row and keeps the best settings on the
module:

```{r}
optimize_grid(
  classify,
  data = reviews,
  metric = metric_exact_match(field = "sentiment"),
  grid = dials::grid_regular(temperature(), levels = 3),
  # gpt-6-luna accepts temperature only with reasoning turned off
  .llm = ellmer::chat_openai(
    model = "gpt-6-luna",
    params = ellmer::params(reasoning_effort = "none")
  )
)
module_trials(classify)
```

To tune how much a reasoning model thinks instead, sweep a `reasoning_effort()`
grid; see [Models, providers and streaming](models-and-providers.html).

## The parsnip model

When `parsnip` is loaded, dsprrr registers a model type, `llm_predict()`, with
the `"dsprrr"` engine for classification and regression:

```{r parsnip-spec}
#| eval: !expr has_parsnip
library(parsnip)

reviews <- tibble::tibble(
  text = c("Arrived broken.", "Works great.", "It's a chair."),
  sentiment = factor(c("negative", "positive", "neutral"))
)

spec <- llm_predict(
  mode = "classification",
  signature = "text -> sentiment: enum('negative', 'neutral', 'positive')",
  temperature = 0
) |>
  set_engine("dsprrr")

fitted <- fit_xy(spec, x = reviews["text"], y = reviews$sentiment)
fitted
```

Fitting builds a zero-shot module from `signature` (or, without one, derives
it from the predictor names and outcome levels), stores `temperature` and
`top_p` in the module's config, and makes no model calls. Use `fit_xy()` (or
`workflows::add_variables()`) rather than a formula for free-text columns: R's
formula interface converts character predictors into factors with fixed
training levels, which rejects unseen text at prediction time.

`predict()` runs the module on `new_data` using the default Chat (set with
`set_default_chat()` or `local_lm()`) and returns `.pred_class` (preserving
the training factor's levels) or `.pred`:

```{r}
set_default_chat(
  ellmer::chat_openai(
    model = "gpt-6-luna",
    params = ellmer::params(reasoning_effort = "none")
  )
)
predict(fitted, new_data = tibble::tibble(text = c("Best purchase ever!", "Total junk.")))
#> # A tibble: 2 x 1
#>   .pred_class
#>   <fct>
#> 1 positive
#> 2 negative
```

For evaluation with graded or repeated samples, see
[Evaluate with vitals](vitals-recipes.html).
